_comment: Project-scoped MCP servers for this repository. Two of them, and they do
different jobs -- see docs/agents.md for why, and for the walkthrough.
serena: generic symbol operations -- find_symbol, find_referencing_symbols,
rename_symbol, safe_delete_symbol -- over an Elixir language server.
Serena is GPL-3.0+ and is not linked, imported or vendored here; this is a
path handed to a separate published process. bin/serena-mcp starts it,
and puts our Expert build ahead of the version Serena would download.
Two things it needs that are easy to miss: the project must be COMPILED
(.serena/project.yml runs `mix compile` on activation), and cross-file
answers need about ten seconds of indexing after that before they are
right.
ash_agent_tools: the DSL half -- the input contract for an action, the
constraints on an attribute, what is declared at a file position. A
language server cannot answer any of those, because Ash declarations are
data in a DSL rather than named symbols. It is NOT an MCP server yet: it
is reached by running bin/ash-agent, which wraps the Mix tasks and prints
JSON. .claude/settings.json allowlists it so it runs without a prompt.
TODO(mix ash_agent.serve): an MCP daemon for these tools is being built
in a parallel lane -- a supervised Bandit on 127.0.0.1:4100, read-only,
started by its own Mix task rather than mounted in this application.
When it lands, start it, delete the bin/ash-agent entries from
.claude/settings.json, and add here, under mcpServers:
"ash_agent": { "type": "http", "url": "http://localhost:4100/mcp" }
Confirm the port and the mount path against the daemon as shipped; 4100
is from its design brief and the path is not fixed there. The tool
surface is the same either way -- describe, validate, search, context,
laws -- so nothing else about this wiring changes.
tidewave and ash_ai_dev are deliberately absent. Both attach to a running
dev server, and both are dependencies this demo does not have: it is a
standalone application, not the ash_enterprise reference app. Add them
only if you add the dependencies.
${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.} covers the two ways a client launches a project
server. If yours does neither, replace it with an absolute path.
